title: I asked Codex to redesign my homepage. It pushed my entire repo to an OpenAI server.
excerpt: Asked to redesign one page, Codex provisioned a git remote on an OpenAI-operated host and pushed my full branch history to it. The approval prompt described this as publishing to 'a private production preview.'
content_html:
I asked OpenAI's Codex to redesign the homepage of this site, and the entire session was three prompts long, all of them about a homepage. At the end of the second one, without any prompting from me, it created a git remote on a host called git.chatgpt-team.site, committed my code and pushed my entire branch history to it.

Everything below comes from the session transcript that Codex writes into ~/.codex/sessions/, which I went through line by line after the fact.

The three prompts

Verbatim, in order:

  1. plan ui improvement of the homepage … discuss and plan
  2. implement
  3. http://localhost:3001/about - use image bhanu.jpeg

Codex answered the first prompt with a design plan, which I read through and approved. It opens:

The best concept is "First Light": Bhanu as the sun, with hope represented by light gradually emerging from darkness.

and it continues through five sections, namely recommended art direction, hero direction, page progression, a 3D implementation plan and a list of things to avoid, and it ends with the line "No files have been changed yet."

The words deploy, host, publish and push do not appear anywhere in it, and neither does any mention of a remote, a site or an OpenAI service, as the plan I approved was a plan about gradients and camera movement. I have reproduced it in full at the end of this post, so you do not have to take my word for the same.

What it did

During the implement turn, without any further prompt from my side, the following happened:

1. It provisioned a remote repository. Codex called an internal Sites tool (_create_site), which returned a git remote along with an auth token:

remote_url: https://git.chatgpt-team.site/…/appgprj_….git
branch:     main
token:      art_v1_…        (redacted)
provider:   cloudflare_artifact

2. It wrote .openai/hosting.json into my repo, which pointed at that newly created project.

3. It committed.

git commit -m "Redesign homepage around the Bhanu solar identity"
[main 0e41226] 5 files changed, 421 insertions(+), 53 deletions(-)

4. It pushed.

git -c http.extraHeader='Authorization: Bearer art_v1_…' \
    push https://git.chatgpt-team.site/…/appgprj_….git HEAD:main

HEAD:main is the part which needs to be read closely, as it does not push the five changed files but every single commit reachable from HEAD, which is to say the whole branch history, to that remote.

That host is reachable from anywhere and it asks for credentials, so it is certainly not a local preview endpoint.

"The model already had your code" is a different claim

This is the first objection that comes up, and it is worth answering precisely instead of dismissing it.

If you use a hosted model, your files do go to someone else's computer, that is true, that is the deal and I took it knowingly. Files are sent as a part of a request, they are processed and they are answered.

A git push, however, is a different operation altogether:

  • Scope. Inference sends whatever the model read, whereas a push of HEAD:main sends every object reachable from HEAD, including files that no model ever opened and commits from years before the session.
  • Persistence. A request is served and it returns, whereas a push creates a repository which continues to exist on that host.
  • Destination. I chose to use Codex, I did not choose git.chatgpt-team.site, and I had not even heard of that host before reading my own logs.
  • Credential. The push authenticated with a bearer token which was minted during the turn and which I never saw until I read the transcript.

I am not arguing that a coding agent should not read my files, as reading them is quite literally the job. What I am arguing is that "read this repo to help me" and "keep a copy of this repo" are two entirely different consents, and only one of the two was ever on the table.

Why it did it

So why did it do any of this? Well, this was not a rogue action at all, it is actually the documented default.

Codex ships with bundled instruction packs, and the one covering websites (sites-building) directs the agent to build, validate and then hand off to hosting "unless the user explicitly asks to keep it local."

So staying local is the opt-out here, which means the safe path is the one you have to ask for. You can only opt out of a pipeline that you know exists, and I did not know the Sites pipeline was in the loop, so I obviously never said the words which would have stopped it.

About the approval

Codex did ask, to be fair to it. It raised escalation prompts for the add, the commit and the push, and I approved every one of them, which I would rather state plainly here than have it pointed out to me later.

The justification text attached to those prompts was:

  • "…publish the exact validated version to a private production preview"
  • "…upload the validated source to the private site repository for deployment"

Set that against the command it was asking to run:

git push https://git.chatgpt-team.site/… HEAD:main

"Private production preview" and "private site repository" both describe a staging environment, whereas the command in front of me was uploading a full source tree along with the complete git history to a git host on the public internet, operated by a third party. The prompt was accurate about the intent and completely silent about the scope, and the scope was the only thing I actually needed to know.

If you want to call that operator error, I will not argue very hard. I would only note that the error here was reading the agent's summary instead of the agent's command, which is exactly the thing these prompts are shaped to encourage.

What HEAD:main actually sends

So what actually leaves your machine when that one command runs? My repo is going public anyway, so in my case this cost me nothing, but let us generalise the same, because quite often the repo in question is not yours to publish:

  • Any secret that was ever committed and later removed is still sitting in the history, and the history is what leaves.
  • Any private or client code in the repo goes along with it.
  • Any unreleased work on a branch reachable from HEAD goes along with it.
  • You do not know the retention, access or training policy for artifacts on that host, simply because you did not know the host was involved in the first place.

What changes I made in my Codex setup

  • State the constraint up front. If a tool has a hosting skill, you should say it at the start of the session itself: keep everything local, do not deploy, do not push to any remote. Make the safe path the one you asked for. If you are using agents.md - mentioning it here should be fine.
  • Read the command, not the justification. For anything which touches the network, look at the destination in the command line, as the friendly description is the agent's summary of its own intent and not a description of what actually runs.
  • Block egress. An agent which cannot reach git.chatgpt-team.site cannot push to it, and a devcontainer with a deny-by-default firewall also handles this.
  • Rotate anything ever committed. "We deleted that key in a later commit" is not protection when the history itself is the payload.
  • Stopped using Codex for anything meaningful. The mitigations above are all mine to maintain, against defaults which I do not control and did not know about. For private repos and client work that trade is simply not worth it, so Codex is off my real projects until the hosting path is opt-in rather than opt-out.

The redesign itself was quite good, incidentally, and that commit is still sitting in my history. The .openai/hosting.json is not.

Appendix: the plan I approved, in full

This is the complete response to prompt 1, reproduced verbatim from the session transcript, down to the line breaks. It is here so that you can check the claim yourself, as nothing in it mentions a remote, a host, a deployment or a push. Read it as the entire basis on which I typed implement.

Codex — response to plan ui improvement of the homepage … discuss and plan

The best concept is “First Light”: Bhanu as the sun, with hope represented by light gradually emerging from darkness.

Recommended art direction

Use a cinematic eclipse rather than a bright solar-system illustration:

  • A huge sun sits in the upper-right background.
  • A dark planet obscures roughly 70% of it, leaving a warm amber corona.
  • Three or four smaller planets appear at the page edges at different depths.
  • Sparse stars, atmospheric dust, and very slow orbital movement add dimension.
  • As the visitor scrolls, the eclipsing planet drifts slightly and reveals more light—hope becoming visible without turning the page bright.
  • The scene should feel sophisticated and architectural, not like a space game.

The overall visual balance should remain approximately:

  • 85% near-black and charcoal
  • 10% muted mocha/copper
  • 5% warm sunlight

Hero direction

Remove the current boxed particle-grid demo. It communicates “generic technology” and separates the visual from the page.

Instead, make the solar scene fill the entire hero background, with the copy floating directly above it on the left.

Suggested copy:

Independent product house

Building useful software for a brighter future.

Bhanu means sun. We build open-source and commercial products that turn difficult problems into useful, dependable tools.

Keep the existing CTAs:

  • Explore the products
  • View the source

The “Bhanu means sun” sentence makes the visual meaningful instead of merely decorative.

Page progression

  1. Hero — First light
    Mostly eclipsed sun, clear positioning, restrained animation.

  2. Products — Worlds in orbit
    Product cards remain readable, but each can receive a subtle planet marker, orbital line, or individual accent color. Avoid making every product literally a planet.

  3. Principles — What guides the work
    Keep the three principles, using faint rays or illuminated borders rather than generic glass effects.

  4. Mission — Toward the light
    The final mission panel can resemble a dawn horizon, with slightly more warmth than the hero. This completes the hope narrative.

  5. Footer — Return to darkness
    Quiet, minimal, near-black.

3D implementation plan

I recommend a real-time, code-native 3D scene rather than a large video:

  • Build a fullscreen SolarScene using Three.js with React Three Fiber.
  • Use simple procedural materials—no heavy texture downloads.
  • Fake most of the solar glow with layered gradients or sprites rather than expensive post-processing bloom.
  • Add very gentle pointer parallax and scroll-based camera movement.
  • Keep the scene behind all content with pointer-events: none.
  • Give mobile a simplified scene with fewer objects.
  • Provide a CSS radial-gradient fallback while WebGL loads or when it is unavailable.
  • Respect prefers-reduced-motion by rendering a static composition.
  • Cap pixel density and pause rendering when the tab is hidden.

Important restraint

I would avoid:

  • Bright yellow covering large portions of the screen
  • Fast planet orbits
  • Dense star fields
  • Lens flares
  • A scientifically accurate solar system
  • Putting moving objects behind body text
  • Turning every section into a different space effect

The homepage still needs to say “serious independent product house” first. The space scene supplies identity, emotion, and memory.

No files have been changed yet. My recommendation is to proceed with the eclipse-to-dawn direction and prototype the hero first before extending the scene through the rest of the homepage.

Five sections about gradients, orbits and camera movement, ending in an explicit statement that nothing had been touched yet. The next word I typed was implement, and I meant it to apply to the list above.

content_html_zh:
我要求 OpenAI 的 Codex 重新设计这个网站的主页，整个会议有 3 个提示，全部都是关于一个主页的。 在第二个结束时，在没有任何提示的情况下，它在名为 git.chatgpt-team.site 的主机上创建了一个 git 远程服务器，提交了我的代码并将我的整个分支历史记录推送到了它。

下面的所有内容都来自 Codex 写入 ~/.codex/sessions/ 的会话记录，我事后逐行查看了该记录。

三个提示

逐字逐句，按顺序：

  1. 计划主页的用户界面改进... 讨论和计划
  2. 实施
  3. http://localhost:3001/about - 使用图像 bhanu.jpeg

Codex 用设计计划回答了第一个提示，我通读并批准了该计划。 它打开：

最好的概念是“第一道光”：巴努是太阳，光明代表希望，逐渐从黑暗中显现出来。

它继续通过五个部分，即推荐的艺术方向、英雄方向、页面进度、3D实施计划和要避免的事情列表，并以“尚未更改文件”结束。

部署、托管、发布和推送这些词没有出现在其中的任何地方，也没有提到远程、站点或 OpenAI 服务，因为我批准的计划是关于梯度和相机移动的计划。 我在这篇文章的末尾完整地复制了它，所以你不必相信我的话。

它做了什么

在机具转动过程中，在我这边没有任何进一步提示的情况下，发生了以下情况：

1. 它配置了一个远程存储库。 Codex 调用了一个内部站点工具 (_create_site)，它返回一个 git 远程以及一个身份验证令牌：

remote_url: https://git.chatgpt-team.site/…/appgprj_….git
branch:     main
token:      art_v1_…        (redacted)
provider:   cloudflare_artifact

2. 它将 .openai/hosting.json 写入我的存储库，该存储库指向新创建的项目。

3. 它承诺了。

git commit -m "Redesign homepage around the Bhanu solar identity"
[main 0e41226] 5 files changed, 421 insertions(+), 53 deletions(-)

4. 它推动了。

git -c http.extraHeader='Authorization: Bearer art_v1_…' \
    push https://git.chatgpt-team.site/…/appgprj_….git HEAD:main

HEAD:main 是需要仔细阅读的部分，因为它不会推送五个更改的文件，而是将 HEAD 中的每个提交（即整个分支历史记录）推送到该远程。

该主机可以从任何地方访问，并且需要凭据，因此它肯定不是本地预览端点。

“模型已经有你的代码”是一个不同的说法

这是出现的第一个反对意见，值得准确回答而不是驳回它。

如果您使用托管模型，您的文件确实会转到其他人的计算机上，这是真的，这就是交易，我是故意接受的。 文件作为请求的一部分发送、处理并得到答复。

然而，git push 是完全不同的操作：

  • 范围。 推理会发送模型读取的任何内容，而 HEAD:main 的推送会发送可从 HEAD 访问的每个对象，包括模型从未打开过的文件以及会话之前几年提交的文件。
  • 坚持。 请求被服务并返回，而推送创建一个存储库，该存储库继续存在于该主机上。
  • 目的地。 我选择使用 Codex，没有选择 git.chatgpt-team.site，在阅读自己的日志之前我什至没有听说过该主机。
  • 凭据。 推送使用不记名令牌进行身份验证，该令牌是在回合期间铸造的，直到我阅读文字记录之前我从未看到过该令牌。

我并不是说编码代理不应该读取我的文件，因为读取它们实际上就是工作。 我要争论的是，“阅读此存储库以帮助我”和“保留此存储库的副本”是两个完全不同的同意，并且这两个同意中只有一个被摆在桌面上。

为什么它这样做

那么它为什么要这么做呢？ 嗯，这根本不是流氓行为，它实际上是记录在案的默认行为。

Codex 附带捆绑的指令包，涵盖网站（站点构建）的指令包指示代理进行构建、验证，然后移交给托管，“除非用户明确要求将其保留在本地”。

因此，留在当地是一种选择，这意味着您必须寻求安全的道路。 您只能选择退出您知道存在的管道，而我不知道站点管道处于循环中，因此我显然从未说过会阻止它的话语。

关于审批

公平地说，食品法典委员会确实提出了要求。 它提出了添加、提交和推送的升级提示，我批准了每一项，我宁愿在这里清楚地说明这一点，也不愿稍后向我指出。

这些提示所附的理由文本是：

  • “……将经过精确验证的版本发布到私人生产预览中”
  • “...将经过验证的源上传到私有站点存储库以进行部署”

根据它要求运行的命令进行设置：

git push https://git.chatgpt-team.site/… HEAD:main

“私有生产预览”和“私有站点存储库”都描述了一个暂存环境，而我前面的命令是将完整的源代码树以及完整的 git 历史记录上传到公共互联网上由第三方运营的 git 主机。 提示对于意图是准确的，对于范围完全没有提及，而范围是我真正需要知道的唯一事情。

如果你想称那个操作员错误，我不会争论得很激烈。 我只想指出，这里的错误是读取代理的摘要而不是代理的命令，这正是这些提示旨在鼓励的事情。

HEAD:main 实际发送什么

那么，当该命令运行时，您的机器实际上会留下什么？ 无论如何，我的回购协议都会公开，所以就我而言，这没有花费我任何费用，但让我们概括一下，因为通常有问题的回购协议不是您可以发布的：

  • 任何曾经犯下并后来被消除的秘密仍然留在历史中，而历史就是留下的。
  • 存储库中的任何私有或客户端代码都随之而来。
  • 从 HEAD 可到达的分支上的任何未发布的工作都会随之而来。
  • 您不知道该主机上工件的保留、访问或培训策略，只是因为您一开始并不知道该主机参与其中。

我对 Codex 设置做了哪些更改

  • 预先说明约束条件。 如果一个工具具有托管技能，您应该在会话本身开始时说：将所有内容保留在本地，不要部署，不要推送到任何远程。 使安全路径成为您所要求的路径。 如果您正在使用agents.md - 在这里提及它应该没问题。
  • 阅读命令，而不是理由。 对于任何涉及网络的内容，请查看命令行中的目标，因为友好的描述是代理对其自身意图的总结，而不是对实际运行内容的描述。
  • 阻止出口。 无法到达 git.chatgpt-team.site 的代理无法推送到它，并且具有默认拒绝防火墙的 devcontainer 也可以处理此问题。
  • 轮换曾经犯过的任何事情。 当历史记录本身是有效负载时，“我们在以后的提交中删除了该密钥”并不是保护。
  • 停止使用 Codex 来做任何有意义的事情。 上述缓解措施都是我维护的，针对我无法控制且不知道的默认情况。 对于私人仓库和客户工作来说，这种交易根本不值得，因此 Codex 不在我的实际项目中，直到托管路径选择加入而不是选择退出。

顺便说一句，重新设计本身非常好，而且那个承诺仍然存在于我的历史中。 .openai/hosting.json 不是。

推荐艺术指导

使用电影般的日食而不是明亮的太阳系插图：

  • 右上方的背景中有一颗巨大的太阳。
  • 一颗黑暗的行星遮蔽了大约 70% 的区域，留下了温暖的琥珀色日冕。
  • 三到四个较小的行星出现在页面边缘不同深度的地方。
  • 稀疏的恒星、大气尘埃和非常缓慢的轨道运动增加了维度。
  • 当参观者滚动时，食行星会轻微漂移并显示出更多的光——希望在不翻页的情况下变得可见。
  • 场景应该感觉复杂且有建筑感，而不是像太空游戏。

整体视觉平衡应保持在大约：

  • 85% 接近黑色和木炭色
  • 10% 柔和的摩卡/铜色
  • 5%温暖的阳光

英雄方向

删除当前盒装粒子网格演示。 它传达“通用技术”并将视觉效果与页面分开。

相反，让太阳场景充满整个英雄背景，副本直接漂浮在其左侧上方。

建议的副本：

独立产品公司为更美好的未来构建有用的软件。 巴努的意思是太阳。 我们构建开源和商业产品，将难题转化为有用、可靠的工具。

保留现有的 CTA：

  • 探索产品
  • 查看源码

“Bhanu 的意思是太阳”这句话使视觉变得有意义，而不仅仅是装饰性的。

页面进展

  1. 英雄 — 第一缕阳光大部分是日食，定位清晰，动画克制。
  2. 产品 — 轨道上的世界 产品卡仍然可读，但每个卡都可以包含微妙的行星标记、轨道线或单独的强调色。 避免让每件产品都成为一个真正的星球。
  3. 原则——指导工作的原则保持三个原则，使用微弱的光线或发光的边框，而不是一般的玻璃效果。
  4. 任务——走向光明最终的任务面板就像黎明的地平线，比英雄稍微温暖一些。 这样就完成了希望的叙述。
  5. 页脚 — 回归黑暗安静、极简、近乎黑色。

3D实施计划

我推荐实时、代码原生的 3D 场景，而不是大型视频：

  • 使用 Three.js 和 React Three Fiber 构建全屏 SolarScene。
  • 使用简单的程序材质——无需下载大量纹理。
  • 使用分层渐变或精灵来模拟大部分太阳光，而不是昂贵的后处理绽放。
  • 添加非常柔和的指针视差和基于滚动的相机移动。
  • 使用指针事件将场景保留在所有内容后面：无。
  • 为移动设备提供更少对象的简化场景。
  • 在 WebGL 加载或不可用时提供 CSS 径向渐变后备。
  • 尊重更喜欢通过渲染静态构图来减少运动。
  • 隐藏选项卡时限制像素密度并暂停渲染。

重要约束

我会避免：

  • 亮黄色覆盖了屏幕的大部分区域
  • 快速行星轨道
  • 密集星域
  • 镜头光晕
